verses.text: Brothers, if someone is caught in a trespass, you who are spiritual should restore him with a spirit of gentleness. But watch yourself, or you also may be tempted.
Carry one another's burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.
If anyone thinks he is something when he is nothing, he deceives himself.
Each one should test his own work. Then he will have reason to boast in himself alone, and not in someone else.
For each one should carry his own load.
Nevertheless, the one who receives instruction in the word must share in all good things with his instructor.
Do not be deceived: God is not to be mocked. Whatever a man sows, he will reap in return.
The one who sows to please his flesh, from the flesh will reap destruction; but the one who sows to please the Spirit, from the Spirit will reap eternal life.
Let us not grow weary in well-doing, for in due time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up.
Therefore, as we have opportunity, let us do good to everyone, and especially to the family of faith.
See what large letters I am using to write to you with my own hand!
Those who want to make a good impression outwardly are trying to compel you to be circumcised. They only do this to avoid persecution for the cross of Christ.
For the circumcised do not even keep the law themselves, yet they want you to be circumcised that they may boast in your flesh.
But as for me, may I never boast, except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.
For neither circumcision nor uncircumcision means anything. What counts is a new creation.
Peace and mercy to all who walk by this rule, even to the Israel of God.
From now on let no one cause me trouble, for I bear on my body the marks of Jesus.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers. Amen.

context.author: Paul the apostle (1:1; 5:2)
context.genre: Letter, urgent and argumentative, with no thanksgiving at the start
context.audience: The churches in Galatia, founded on Paul’s first journey
context.setting: Paul gives practical advice for the church. He tells the strong to restore those who fall gently, to carry one another’s burdens, and to give generously. Then he takes the pen himself and writes the last lines in large letters, warning that the agitators want to boast in the Galatians’ circumcision, while he boasts only in the cross.
context.custom: Letters were dictated to a scribe and the author often added a few lines in his own hand as a signature. Paul’s “large letters” (v.11) may reflect poor eyesight or emphasis. “The marks of Jesus” (v.17) were scars from beatings.
context.timelineImmediate: The letter ends. Paul’s mission continued, and the Jerusalem council settled the question for the churches (Acts 15).
context.timelineBible: “A man reaps what he sows” (v.7) is a common wisdom saying (Job 4:8; Proverbs 22:8; Hosea 10:12). The “Israel of God” (v.16) points to the people of the new covenant.
context.sparkNotes: If someone is caught in a sin, restore him gently. Carry each other’s burdens, which fulfills the law of Christ. Whoever sows to the flesh reaps corruption, and whoever sows to the Spirit reaps eternal life. Let us not grow weary in doing good. Paul warns about those who want to compel circumcision to avoid persecution, and boasts only in the cross of Christ. A new creation is what counts.

translation.meaning: Heavy loads. Paul uses another word in v.5 for each one’s own pack, which is a different thing.
A wholly new work of God, the same phrase as in 2 Corinthians 5:17.

otBackground.note: Those who plow evil reap the same.
Peace on Israel, behind the “Israel of God.”

overview.summary: Believers should restore, carry burdens, and do good. Paul closes by boasting only in the cross, where the world was crucified to him, and what counts is a new creation.
overview.settingLine: Paul writes to the churches of Galatia.

history.t: He wrote the end of many letters (1 Cor 16:21; Col 4:18; 2 Thess 3:17).
Paul had been beaten and stoned in Lystra (Acts 14:19).

customs.t: Slaves and temple servants were sometimes marked. Paul says his scars show whom he serves.
Teachers could count converts as a proof of success.

archaeology.t: Surviving papyrus letters show how a scribe wrote and the sender signed.
Acts 14:19 says Paul was stoned at Lystra. Some scholars link the "marks of Jesus" in 6:17 to beatings like that, but Paul does not say what the marks were.

overview.discussion: Paul says to “carry each other’s burdens.” Who is carrying something heavy near me, and what small thing could I do this week?
overview.book: The letter to the Galatians · 6 chapters. Paul’s sharpest defense of freedom in Christ.
overview.author: Paul

historicalImage.caption: The Gleaners, by Jean-François Millet (1857), in the Musée d'Orsay. Paul tells the Galatians not to grow weary in doing good, because in due time they will reap if they do not give up, and to do good to everyone, above all to the household of faith (Galatians 6:9-10). The law of Moses left the edges of the field for the poor to glean (Leviticus 19:9-10).
